Zalando changed Zalando Plus from a paid membership to a free-to-join model with a points-based system, and it recognised accruals for reimbursing Zalando Plus subscription fees to customers at the beginning of 2025.

- The programme was evolved in 2024 into a points-based system rewarding customer loyalty, moving from a paid membership to a free-to-join model (Group strategy; Key intangible resources; Accounting policies).
- Points earned unlock four benefit levels, with perks like birthday vouchers and exclusive events; the new approach was tested in Spain and expanded to France and Austria, with further rollout in 2025 (Group strategy; Foreword).
- Under the accounting policies, the awards create a separate performance obligation providing a material right to customers (Accounting policies).
- Among other current non-financial liabilities, the report mentions increased accruals for the reimbursement of Zalando Plus subscription fees to customers at the beginning of 2025, included in "others" (Notes 9.–26.).

Delivery Hero treats the two periods differently: the pre-August 2021 model risk is deemed probable, so provisions are recognized, while the post-August 2021 model risk is deemed possible but not probable, so it is disclosed only as a contingency. Glovo decided to progressively move to an employment-based model in Spain from 2025.

- Provisions are reflected for risks in Spain relating to the model operated by Glovo until August 2021, as it is more likely than not that the risk materializes (Strategic Risks, [1]).
- For Glovo Spain after August 2021, the rider risk is deemed possible but not probable and is disclosed as a contingency, with a contingent liability of €440 to 770 million for the Spanish social security investigation into the model since August 2021 (Strategic Risks [1]; Auditor's Report [2]; Contingencies [3]).
- No provision was recognized for the post-2021 model because reclassification by Spanish courts was assessed as not probable, though the courier fleet was reclassified to employee status in January 2025 (Contingencies, [3]).
- In December 2024, Glovo's management decided to progressively move to an employment-based model in Spain effective 2025 to avoid further legal uncertainties, while Glovo will defend the self-employed status through all available instances and continue cooperating with Spanish authorities (Strategic Risks [4]; CEO letter [6]).

Vodafone Turkey - 2G licence extension: €120 million for a six-year extension until 30 April 2029 (excluding 18% VAT), paid in advance with a capital injection.
Turkcell - 2G licence extension: EUR 120 million (plus EUR 21.6 million of value-added taxes), paid in installments — an initial payment of EUR 81.6 million (TRY 1.7 billion) in 2023, approximately half of the remaining installments (EUR 31.1 million, TRY 1.1 billion) in April 2024, with the remaining amount to be paid within a year.

Both agreed to the same €120 million fee (excluding VAT) for extension to 30 April 2029, but Vodafone Turkey paid the fee in advance via a capital injection, whereas Turkcell paid in installments in Turkish Lira over 2023–2025.

Zalando - end of 2022: EUR 304.3m committed to further invest in fulfilment centres
Zalando - end of 2024: 59.5m EUR committed to invest a further in fulfilment centres

The commitment fell by EUR 244.8m (304.3 − 59.5) between the end of 2022 and the end of 2024.

Zalando - 2024: KPMG AG Wirtschaftsprüfungsgesellschaft, Berlin (new in 2024; prior year auditor was EY GmbH & Co. KG, Stuttgart)
Delivery Hero - 2024: KPMG AG Wirtschaftsprüfungsgesellschaft, Berlin (appointed by the 2024 Annual General Meeting for financial year 2024)

Yes, both companies used the same auditor, KPMG AG Wirtschaftsprüfungsgesellschaft, Berlin, for their 2024 financial statements. For Zalando it was new in 2024 due to legal rotation (replacing EY), while for Delivery Hero KPMG was appointed by the 2024 AGM, so it was also newly appointed for 2024.
